follow-up time: From caesarean section to determination of surgical site infection occurrence.
study type: multicentre, pragmatic, randomised, controlled, parallel group, superiority trial
exposure: closed incision negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT)
outcome: wound complications (dehiscence, haematoma, seroma, bleeding, bruising)
cohort: 2035 obese women (BMI >= 30) undergoing elective or semi-urgent caesarean section at four Australian tertiary hospitals.
finding: While not statistically significant, closed incision NPWT in obese women post-caesarean section showed a 24% risk reduction in SSI compared to standard dressings, but increased skin blistering.
mod_finding: Closed incision negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) for obese women after caesarean section resulted in a 24% reduction in the risk of SSI (3% reduction in absolute risk) compared with standard dressings.
who: Obese mothers who underwent caesarean section
